newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU proposes joint Mideast peace bid with U.S.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes joint Mideast peace bid with U.S.

text.p: The European Union has agreed to propose to the United States taking a joint initiative to revive troubled Middle East peace negotiations, France said on Tuesday.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux was reporting on a meeting of Middle East department heads of the 15 EU member states with the bloc's special envoy to the region, Miguel Angel Moratinos, in Brussels on Monday.

"They agreed to propose that the Netherlands prime minister (Wim Kok) as current president of the European Union write to President (Bill) Clinton to propose a joint American-European initiative," Doutriaux told reporters.

The move came after Clinton and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu apparently failed in frank talks in Washington on Monday to overcome differences over the building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem that have stymied Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
Netanyahu rebuffed all calls for a settlements freeze and said Israel would not surrender to "terrorism".
Doutriaux said the Europeans' ideas were "complementary to and in convergence with the Americans".

"Our proposals are aimed at taking account of all outstanding questions to try to lay the foundations for a global restarting of negotiations between the Israelis and the Palestinians," he told a regular briefing.
"They also aim to take account of the need to ensure that past agreements are respected (as well as responding to the crucial security concern which we share)," he said.
He said Moratinos had offered a "code of conduct to restore the dynamics of dialogue" but gave no details.

The spokesman reaffirmed that France sought a freeze on all Jewish settlements and a halt to construction work on the Har Homa housing project which triggered the latest wave of violent Palestinian protests against Israel.
French officials said that President Jacques Chirac's diplomatic adviser, Jean-David Levitte, had talks with U.S. special Middle East envoy Dennis Ross in Washington on Monday.
